question: Which of the following is an Indian martial art that originated in modern-day Kerala?
solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Kalaripayattu.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Indian martial art **known as **Kalaripayattu **was developed in** Kerala** in the present day.
 
• The **Vadakkan Pattukal**, a compilation of ballads about the** Chekavar of Kerala's Malabar area,** makes reference to Kalaripayattu.
 
• The main premise of **Kalaripayattu,** according to the Vadakkan Pattukal, is that knowledge of the art should be applied to further deserving causes rather than **one's own self-interests.**
 
• Kalaripayattu is a **martial art with weapons** and** fighting methods** that are exclusive to Kerala that were created for th**e ancient battlefield.**
 
• **Hinduism **served as inspiration for the** rituals and ideologies **seen in Kalaripayattu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Muay Thai:**

 
 
• **Thai boxing** is another name for muay thai.
 
• It is a combat sport that combines various **clinching maneuvers **with stand-up hitting.
 
• The **"art of eight limbs"** is the name given to this profession.
 
 
 
• **Karate:**
 
 
• A martial technique called karate was created in the **Ryukyu Kingdom**.
 
• Under the influence o**f Chinese martial arts,** it evolved from the local Ryukyuan martial arts.
 
 
 
• **Gatka:**
 
 
• **The Sikhs of the Punjab **are particularly identified with the martial technique known as gatka.
 
• It's a** form of stick fighting **where the wooden sticks are used to represent swords.
